---
title: "Positional Encoding"
---

## Why Position Information Is Necessary

Self-attention alone is permutation-equivariant: permuting the input tokens
permutes the outputs in the same way. The attention score $q_i^T k_j$ contains
content similarity, but it does not inherently say whether token $j$ comes
before or after token $i$, or how far apart they are.

This statement needs one qualification: a **causal mask is itself tied to
sequence order**. Although it does not attach an explicit coordinate to a token,
it gives different positions different visible prefixes. This asymmetry is what
makes NoPE possible in decoder-only Transformers.

Position information can be introduced by:

- adding a position-dependent vector to each token representation
- modifying attention scores with a position-dependent bias
- transforming queries and keys as a function of their positions

> **Learning prompt:** Precisely distinguish permutation equivariance from
> permutation invariance. Which one describes self-attention?

## NoPE: No Explicit Positional Encoding

**NoPE** removes the explicit positional mechanism entirely:

$$
x_i=E_{\text{token}}[w_i],
\qquad
S_{ij}=\frac{q_i^T k_j}{\sqrt{d_h}}.
$$

There is no additive position embedding, relative-position bias, or RoPE
rotation. A decoder still applies its causal mask:

$$
\widetilde S_{ij}
=
\begin{cases}
S_{ij}, & j\le i,\\
-\infty, & j>i.
\end{cases}
$$

Thus the visible set at position $i$ is the prefix
$\{1,\ldots,i\}$. Position is not supplied as a feature; it can emerge from the
structure of the computation.

### How can order emerge from only a causal mask?

At layer $\ell$, position $i$ aggregates representations only from its prefix:

$$
h_i^{(\ell+1)}
=
F\!\left(
h_i^{(\ell)},
\left\{h_j^{(\ell)}:j\le i\right\}
\right).
$$

Each earlier representation already summarizes a **different nested prefix**.
Consequently, a multi-layer model can distinguish orders that one content-only
attention layer cannot.

Consider `A B C` and `B A C`. At `C`, a first layer sees the same multiset
`{A, B, C}` in either sequence, so its direct content aggregation can be the
same. But the earlier states differ:

```text
A B C:  h_A sees {A};    h_B sees {A, B}
B A C:  h_B sees {B};    h_A sees {B, A}
```

At the next layer, `C` attends to these already contextualized states and can
distinguish the two orders. This is why the depth qualification matters: causal
connectivity can carry order through the network even though the token
embeddings contain no position.

The model may also infer approximate absolute position from signals correlated
with prefix length, such as its number of predecessors, special anchor tokens,
or changes in attention-output statistics. Probing experiments find recoverable
absolute-position information in trained NoPE models. However, the causal mask
does not hand the model an exact integer $i$; learning a useful coordinate is an
emergent behavior, not a guaranteed primitive.

### What the causal mask does and does not provide

| Property | Causal NoPE |
|---|---|
| Which tokens are in the past? | supplied by the triangular connectivity pattern |
| Exact absolute index $i$ | not supplied explicitly; may be inferred |
| Exact distance $i-j$ | not supplied explicitly; may be represented by deeper computation |
| Order sensitivity | possible in multi-layer autoregressive Transformers |
| Bidirectional encoder order | not recovered from a full, symmetric attention mask alone |
| Extra position parameters or rotations | none |

So the answer to “does causal masking fully encode position?” is **no**. It
breaks permutation symmetry and exposes an ordered prefix structure from which
the model can learn position. That is weaker and less direct than providing an
absolute or relative coordinate.

### Minimal implementation

NoPE is implemented mostly by omission: do not add a position table and do not
transform $Q$ or $K$.

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def nope_attention(q: torch.Tensor,
                   k: torch.Tensor,
                   v: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Causal NoPE attention for q, k, v shaped (B, H, T, D)."""
    return F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
        q, k, v,
        attn_mask=None,
        is_causal=True,
    )
```

KV caching still works. Cached keys need no position-dependent rotation, but the
harness or attention kernel must still know which cached tokens precede the new
query so it can enforce causality.

### Why use or avoid NoPE?

| Potential advantage | Potential limitation |
|---|---|
| no position parameters or rotation cost | weaker positional inductive bias |
| no learned position table with a fixed maximum index | training must discover useful order and distance features |
| no RoPE frequencies that move out of their training regime | exact position-sensitive tasks may be harder |
| strong length generalization on some reasoning tasks | results are architecture- and task-dependent |
| especially natural for causal decoders | not a direct solution for bidirectional attention |

[Haviv et al. (2022)](https://aclanthology.org/2022.findings-emnlp.99/)
found that causal language models without explicit positional encodings can be
competitive and develop probe-decodable absolute position. In controlled
reasoning experiments,
[Kazemnejad et al. (2023)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/hash/4e85362c02172c0c6567ce593122d31c-Abstract-Conference.html)
found that NoPE generalized to longer sequences better than several explicit
alternatives. These findings establish possibility, not a universal claim that
NoPE always beats RoPE or relative bias.

### Recent update: frontier models use hybrid NoPE

The important production shift is not that frontier models have universally
removed positional encoding from every layer. The clearer 2025--2026 trend is
to give different layer types different positional roles. One important form
**interleaves RoPE and NoPE layers**:

$$
\operatorname{Attn}_{\ell}
=
\begin{cases}
\operatorname{LocalAttn}(R_iq_i,R_jk_j,V),
& \ell\notin\mathcal L_{\text{NoPE}},\\
\operatorname{GlobalAttn}(Q,K,V),
& \ell\in\mathcal L_{\text{NoPE}}.
\end{cases}
$$

This is a division of labor:

- **local RoPE layers** provide a strong inductive bias for nearby order and
  relative distance
- **global NoPE layers** communicate across the full context without applying a
  position-dependent rotation outside its familiar training regime
- depth lets the global layer operate on token states that have already acquired
  local order information from earlier RoPE layers

A second form replaces the local RoPE layers with an **ordered recurrent or
linear-attention mechanism**. The recurrence itself is position-sensitive, so
global full-attention layers can use NoPE without making the entire network
permutation-invariant. Kimi K3 is the frontier-scale example below.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    X[Token states] --> R1[Local RoPE]
    R1 --> R2[Local RoPE]
    R2 --> R3[Local RoPE]
    R3 --> N[Global NoPE]
    N --> Y[Repeat the block]
```

This hybrid is easier to understand as **two communication scales** than as a
vote over which positional encoding is universally best. RoPE answers “where is
this token relative to nearby tokens?” Global NoPE answers “which content
anywhere in the prefix is relevant?”

#### Llama 4: iRoPE

Meta calls Llama 4's design **iRoPE**, for interleaved RoPE and NoPE. Meta states
that most layers retain RoPE while some attention layers omit positional
embeddings to improve length generalization. The released reference
implementation marks every fourth layer as NoPE; those layers use global causal
attention, while the intervening RoPE layers use chunked attention.

For an interval $r=4$,

$$
\mathcal L_{\text{NoPE}}
=
\{\ell:(\ell+1)\bmod 4=0\}.
$$

Thus “Llama 4 uses NoPE” does **not** mean all of its attention is position-free:
the repeating pattern is three RoPE layers followed by one NoPE layer. See
Meta's [Llama 4 architecture announcement](https://ai.meta.com/blog/llama-4-multimodal-intelligence/)
and its
[`is_nope_layer` implementation](https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama4/model.py).

#### Apple foundation models

Apple's 2025 foundation models also interleave sliding-window local attention
with RoPE and global attention without positional embeddings. Apple reports this
choice as improving length generalization while maintaining long-context model
quality. See the
[Apple Intelligence Foundation Language Models report](https://machinelearning.apple.com/research/apple-foundation-models-2025-updates).

This is stronger evidence of an architectural pattern than one isolated model:
two frontier-scale model families independently assign explicit position to
local communication and NoPE to global communication.

#### Kimi K3: NoPE global attention after recurrent position mixing

Kimi K3 makes the more substantial switch that motivates much of the recent
NoPE discussion. Kimi K2 and K2.5 used MLA with RoPE, whereas Kimi K3 applies
**NoPE to every global Gated MLA layer**. Its repeating block contains three
Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers followed by one global Gated MLA layer:

$$
\underbrace{\operatorname{KDA}
\rightarrow \operatorname{KDA}
\rightarrow \operatorname{KDA}}_{\text{ordered recurrent mixing}}
\rightarrow
\underbrace{\operatorname{GatedMLA}_{\text{NoPE}}}_{\text{global content routing}}.
$$

This does not mean that Kimi K3 has no notion of position. KDA updates a
recurrent state in token order and uses learned, channel-wise decay, making its
mixing both position-sensitive and recency-aware. The later NoPE MLA layer can
therefore globally retrieve representations that already contain order. No RoPE
frequency needs to be retuned when the context is extended.

This is a useful generalization of the Llama 4 pattern:

| Local or recurrent path | Global path |
|---|---|
| Llama 4: local attention with explicit RoPE | full attention with NoPE |
| Kimi K3: KDA recurrence with implicit, learned positional dynamics | Gated MLA with NoPE |

See the [Kimi K3 technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24653), especially
Sections 2.1 and 3.4.

#### SmolLM3: an open, reproducible example

Hugging Face's 3B SmolLM3 is not frontier-scale, but it provides unusually open
ablation evidence and a practical implementation. It removes RoPE from every
fourth layer and reports improved long-context behavior without hurting
short-context results. Its remaining RoPE layers still use YaRN and adjusted
RoPE frequencies for context extension. Therefore the model is another **hybrid
RoPE--NoPE** design, not a pure NoPE model. See the
[SmolLM3 training report](https://huggingface.co/blog/smollm3).

#### Model map: NoPE is a trend, not a universal switch

| Model family | Position design | Correct interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Llama 4 | local/chunked RoPE; periodic global NoPE | hybrid RoPE--NoPE |
| Apple foundation models (2025) | sliding-window RoPE; global NoPE | hybrid RoPE--NoPE |
| Kimi K3 | three KDA layers; every global Gated MLA layer uses NoPE | recurrent-position + global-NoPE hybrid |
| SmolLM3 | every fourth layer removes RoPE; other layers retain RoPE/YaRN | open small-scale hybrid |
| Qwen3 | RoPE in the architecture; ABF, YaRN, and DCA for long context | not NoPE |
| DeepSeek-V3 | MLA with a decoupled query/key component carrying RoPE | not NoPE |

The last two rows are important counterexamples. Qwen3 explicitly retains RoPE
and raises its base frequency during long-context training; DeepSeek-V3's MLA
compresses content keys and values but keeps a separate RoPE-bearing component.
MLA therefore does **not** imply NoPE. See the
[Qwen3 technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09388) and
[DeepSeek-V3 technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.19437).

### Minimal hybrid implementation

The layer schedule can be implemented by conditionally applying RoPE:

```python
def hybrid_attention(q, k, v, layer_idx, apply_rope, nope_interval=4):
    """Sketch of a 3-RoPE : 1-NoPE schedule."""
    is_nope_layer = (layer_idx + 1) % nope_interval == 0

    if not is_nope_layer:
        q, k = apply_rope(q, k)

    return F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
        q, k, v,
        is_causal=True,
    )
```

This sketch changes only the positional transform. Llama 4 additionally changes
the attention span: RoPE layers are local/chunked and NoPE layers are global.
Kimi K3 instead replaces the RoPE branch with an ordered KDA recurrence. A real
implementation must construct the appropriate mask or recurrent state for each
layer and handle cached positions consistently.

### What changed in our understanding?

| Earlier interpretation | More recent interpretation |
|---|---|
| choose one PE for the entire model | positional strategy can vary by layer |
| NoPE is mainly a surprising ablation | NoPE can be a global-routing component in a production LLM |
| every layer must directly encode distance | local layers can encode order for later global layers |
| context extension is only a RoPE-rescaling problem | architecture can provide a position-free global path |
| NoPE has zero positional signal | it has no **explicit** PE but still inherits causal and contextual order |

Recent theory also sharpens the role of depth. Work on the
[counting power of NoPE Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11199)
finds a large expressivity gap between one and multiple attention layers in a
formal hard-attention setting. This supports the nested-prefix intuition above,
although a theorem about an idealized hard-attention model is not direct evidence
about optimization or quality in a finite-precision frontier LLM.

The practical conclusion is:

$$
\boxed{
\text{modern NoPE trend}
\approx
\text{position-aware local or recurrent mixing}
+
\text{position-free global routing}
}.
$$

## Relative Position Bias

Instead of modifying the input representation, add a position-dependent term
to the attention logits:

$$
S_{ij}
=
\frac{q_i^T k_j}{\sqrt{d_h}} + b(i,j).
$$

## Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE)

RoPE applies a position-dependent rotation to pairs of query and key
dimensions:

$$
q_t' = R_t q_t,
\qquad
k_s' = R_s k_s.
$$

Because rotation matrices are orthogonal,

$$
(q_t')^T k_s'
=
q_t^T R_t^T R_s k_s
=
q_t^T R_{s-t}k_s.
$$

Thus the attention score depends on the relative displacement $s-t$, even
though each query and key is rotated using its absolute position.

## Interview Questions

- Why does self-attention require position information?
- Does the causal mask by itself fully encode token positions?
- What does NoPE remove, and what order-dependent structure remains?
- Why can a multi-layer NoPE decoder distinguish `A B C` from `B A C` even
  when a single content-only attention layer at `C` cannot?
- Why is NoPE more natural for a causal decoder than a bidirectional encoder?
- What length-generalization advantage might NoPE have over a learned position
  table or fixed RoPE frequencies?
- Why do Llama 4 and Apple's foundation models combine local RoPE with global
  NoPE instead of removing RoPE everywhere?
- How can Kimi K3 use NoPE in every global MLA layer while remaining sensitive
  to order? What positional role does KDA play?
- In iRoPE, how can a global NoPE layer remain order-aware after local RoPE
  layers?
- Does saying “Llama 4 uses NoPE” imply that every attention layer is NoPE?
- Why does DeepSeek-V3's use of MLA not imply that it uses NoPE?
- What is the difference between absolute and relative position information?
- How does RoPE make attention scores depend on relative displacement?
- Why must the RoPE head dimension be arranged in pairs?
- What makes context-length extension difficult?
